_README: Copy to config/rates.json, fill in the eight numbers, set `verified`, then:
Every field here is a PRICE, which is an assumption. Every number the report
prints beside them is a MEASURED quantity. Keeping the two apart is the whole
point of this file: a rate baked into the script would become indistinguishable
from a result the moment it went stale.
Set `verified` to the date you last checked these against the vendors' pricing
pages. Until it is set, the report marks every dollar figure with ~ and prints
a warning. That is deliberate — an unverified total is arithmetic, not a cost.
config/rates.json is gitignored: prices are account-specific, and a committed

_note: Three rates, not one. Cached input bills at a discount, and the report
already splits prompt_tokens into cached and uncached — putting the same
number in both fields silently deletes the cache's entire value.
prompt_tokens INCLUDES the cached portion; the report subtracts rather
than adds, so do not pre-net these.

deepgram._note: Streaming nova-3 rate. Billed on audio duration, so it tracks call length, not turn count.

_note: Derive from your plan: monthly price divided by the plan's character
quota gives an effective per-character rate. Overage is priced separately
and is usually dearer, so a call that pushes you past the quota costs more
than this figure suggests.

google_tts._note: Only charged on the ElevenLabs fallback path. Usually 0 chars; non-zero means the voice was degraded, which tts_fallback_turns also counts.

_note: TWO line items, not one: the inbound leg and Media Streams are billed
separately, and forgetting the second understates every call.
Rates differ by country — a UK number and a US number are not the same
price, so this file is per-deployment.
billing_increment_seconds drives round-UP: at 60, a 180.3s call bills as
4 minutes. Set it to your actual increment.
The estate, which costs the same at zero calls as at a thousand. Used ONLY
for the fully-loaded figure, and only when --calls-this-month is passed.
Never price a customer off fully-loaded at low volume: it is dominated by
a fixed cost that does not grow with usage, and it will tell you a viable
product is hopeless.
`other` covers Artifact Registry, KMS, logging and anything else standing.
